Josh, I hear you, but I still think merging is the right move because it simplifies security. A unified error handling mechanism means fewer blind spots, less complexity, and a much more consistent security posture.

**Less Dev Work, Fewer Mistakes** – One mechanism, one place to verify, one secure path. The more scattered the handling, the more likely devs miss something.

**Catches Everything** – Everything funnels through the same controlled process. That’s much stronger security.

**Easier to Test & Audit** – A single, structured approach makes it easier to test, automate, and prove security is solid.

Most frameworks already do this in one shot, and even in custom code, a high-level try/catch around request processing achieves both goals cleanly. More separation just invites inconsistency. The only time I have seen this as a challenge is low quality PHP applications where each endpoint is a separate file, and that went out of style 15 years ago.

And really, if you both think strongly about this, I can let it go. But I really feel the merge is better for a lot of reasons.

As I wrote in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2709#issuecomment-2726313883, displaying error messages and catch all are different test-caseses from verifying point of view and must be in a separate requirements only because of that.

2nd blocker is different levels - (based on proposals) 7.4.1 is L2, and 7.4.3 is L3. I don't want to merge the content 7.4.3 into 7.4.1 to require it from L2.

I don't argue how someone implements it or it is supported or not supported by frameworks, I just explain why those 2 need to be in a separate requirements in ASVS.

I think the underlying problem here is that 7.4.3 does not describe why it exists and what precise security problem it solves, and then everyone can interpret it differently.

In v.4.0.3 we had requirements written as:
* V7.4.2 Verify that exception handling (or a functional equivalent) is used across the codebase to account for expected and unexpected error conditions.
* V7.4.3 Verify that a "last resort" error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions.

We deleted 7.4.2 as "DELETED, INSUFFICIENT IMPACT".

I think the combined point for those 2 is: "to not lose error details for logging and monitoring" - this message should be added to 7.4.3.

> Josh, I hear you, but I still think merging is the right move because it simplifies security. A unified error handling mechanism means fewer blind spots, less complexity, and a much more consistent security posture.

I agree that having a centralised and unified error handling mechanism is a better way of approaching this but I don't think we can mandate it as the **only** way of having a secure app. 

We therefore need to provide the two requirements separately to handle a situation where an application does not do this in a centralised way. This is important for both developers when implementing and also when verifying.

We should however mention this in the recommendations section.

> I think the underlying problem here is that 7.4.3 does not describe why it exists and what precise security problem it solves, and then everyone can interpret it differently.

Maybe we fix this with:

"_Verify that a "last resort" error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions to avoid unexpected crashes **which could lead to loss of availability or disclosure of sensitive crash data**._"
